what_its_for: Idelalisib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including a type of leukemia called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and a type of lymphoma called follicular lymphoma. It works by blocking a protein inside cancer cells that helps them grow and survive, which slows or stops the cancer from spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg taken by mouth twice a day (about every 12 hours). Your doctor may lower your dose or have you take a break from the medicine if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since you were supposed to take it, take the missed dose right away. If it has been more than 6 hours, skip the missed dose completely and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store idelalisib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from moisture and heat. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid starting any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements (especially St. John's Wort) without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, because many medicines can interact with idelalisib. Avoid getting live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) while on this medicine. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can weaken your immune system and make you more likely to get infections. Women of childbearing age and men with female partners of childbearing age must use highly effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe diarrhea or diarrhea that contains blood or mucus; severe stomach pain or cramps; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness; signs of serious lung problems such as new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or difficulty breathing; signs of serious skin reactions such as blistering, peeling, or a widespread rash; fever, chills, or other signs of infection; unusual bleeding or bruising; or if you feel very tired or weak. Also call your doctor if you develop any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Idelalisib may start working within the first few weeks of treatment, but you may not notice visible changes right away. Your doctor will order regular blood tests and checkups to see how the medicine is working. Some patients see improvements in their blood counts or tumor size within the first 1 to 3 months. It is important to keep taking the medicine as directed even if you feel well, and to attend all of your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): This medicine is commonly used in older patients; no dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, so close monitoring is important. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your dose may need to be adjusted or more frequent monitoring may be needed. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney disease. Pregnancy: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm or cause the death of an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking idelalisib and for at least 1 month after the last dose, as it is not known if the medicine passes into breast milk.
